title: Pezeshkian Says Iran Should End War Now 'From a Position of Power and Dignity'
detail: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told a press conference in Tehran that it would be better for Iran to bring the war to an end now, arguing Tehran is negotiating from strength: 'It is better to end the war today, when we are in power and dignity, and the whole world acknowledges our victory.' He added that 'all our commanders and armed forces are fully prepared to defend the country with all their might' if fighting resumes, and stressed that the June memorandum of understanding with the US was 'honourable' and did not amount to capitulation. The remarks came as reports suggested reduced near-term escalation risk, with analysts framing Washington's fresh sanctions push as a delaying tactic ahead of the US midterm elections. Oil traders read the comments as a mild de-escalation signal; Brent crude was 'little changed' near $93-94/bbl in the session.

media.caption: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says Tehran should end the war now while in a 'position of power and dignity'

title: Treasury Vows 'Toughest Sanctions in History' on Iran, Redesignates Hezbollah; China Rebuffs Pressure Campaign
detail: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington will impose 'the toughest sanctions in history' on Iran as part of a 'one-two punch' with the existing naval blockade, previewing details at a Monday press conference. The same day, Treasury amended Hezbollah's sanctions designation to describe it as operating 'in service to the Iranian regime under the command of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Quds Force,' and separately sanctioned 10 individuals in a Lebanon-Turkey-UAE-Iran cash-courier network allegedly moving hundreds of millions of dollars. Bessent urged Beijing — which buys more than 80% of Iran's shipped oil — to 'get with the program,' saying such conversations were 'best to have in private.' China's Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian rejected the pressure the next day, saying 'sanctions and pressure will not help resolve the issue' and that Beijing 'opposes illegal unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law.' Iran's Foreign Ministry called the sanctions 'economic terrorism' targeting ordinary citizens, while VP JD Vance called economic pressure 'the most effective tool.'

media.caption: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent previews 'toughest sanctions in history' on Iran as China rejects the pressure campaign

title: US Gas Prices Hit Highest-Ever Mid-August Level as Trump Says He'll 'Never Apologize' for the Cost of War
detail: AAA's national average for regular gasoline stood at $4.06/gallon, the highest ever recorded for mid-August according to GasBuddy analyst Patrick De Haan — up 92 cents from a year earlier, with diesel hitting a record $5.46-5.47/gallon for the month. California and Hawaii averages neared or topped $5.40/gallon. President Trump defended the cost, telling reporters 'I'll never apologize, I did the right thing' and that Americans paying 'a tiny little bit more for your gasoline' was the price of preventing 'a very evil country' from obtaining a nuclear weapon — a contrast with his campaign pledge of $1.85/gallon gas. CNN's live coverage on Aug 21 noted prices remained elevated as Strait of Hormuz traffic stayed near a trickle, around 20% of the pre-war seven-day average per UKMTO.

media.caption: US gas prices hit their highest-ever mid-August level as the Iran war disrupts Strait of Hormuz shipping
